q: How does Argo CD on the hub know that cell-1 exists?
options: A Secret in the `argocd` namespace labelled `argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster`
why: Argo CD discovers clusters from Secrets labelled `argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster` holding the API address and credentials. `argocd cluster add` is only a shortcut that creates such a Secret; at fleet scale you create them with automation.

q: Why does the clusters generator select `fleet.lab/cell` with `operator: Exists`?
options: To include the hub as a cell
Because Argo CD requires every generator to have a selector
So only cells match: the hub's in-cluster entry has no `fleet.lab/cell` label
To sort the cells by name
why: Without a selector the clusters generator also returns the hub (`in-cluster`). Selecting on a label that only cell Secrets carry keeps workloads off the hub.

q: `kubectl get pods` fails with an error about `localhost:8080` and openapi. What is the most likely cause?
options: `KUBECONFIG` is not set, so kubectl falls back to `localhost:8080`, which on this laptop is Argo CD's port
The cell's API server is overloaded
why: With no kubeconfig, kubectl defaults to `http://localhost:8080`. In this lab that port is the Argo CD UI, so you get confusing errors. Fix: `export KUBECONFIG=~/idp-lab/fleet.kubeconfig`.

q: You must put 100 existing clusters behind one Argo CD. What is the engineering way?
options: Run `argocd cluster add` 100 times by hand
Generate the cluster Secrets (with labels) from an inventory using automation, and let ApplicationSets select on the labels
Install a separate Argo CD in each cluster and stop there
why: Treat clusters as data: an inventory (like `cells.conf`) produces labelled Secrets via Terraform, Crossplane or a script. ApplicationSets then target clusters by label, so adding cluster 101 is one more inventory line.

q: In this lab, what are `cell` and `ring`?
options: Label names we chose: a cell is a workload cluster, a ring is its rollout wave
why: They are conventions. They only mean something because ApplicationSets and RollingSync select on them. You could call them block and flat as long as you change every place that uses them.

q: The fleet ApplicationSet combines which two generators?
options: scmProvider (Gitea org `golden`) × clusters (cells), in a matrix
why: scmProvider finds every repo in the `golden` org; clusters finds every cell. The matrix creates one Application per repo × cell.

q: There are 3 repos with a `deploy/` folder and 2 cells. How many Applications does the fleet ApplicationSet create?
why: Matrix = product: 3 repos × 2 cells = 6 Applications, named `<repo>-<cell>`.

q: What does `filters: [{pathsExist: [deploy]}]` do in the scmProvider generator?
options: Creates a `deploy/` folder in every repo
Only repos that contain a `deploy/` folder produce Applications
Deploys only the files in `deploy/` to the hub
why: It's an opt-in convention: a repo becomes a deployable service by having `deploy/`. Docs repos or libraries in the same org are ignored.

q: Why does the template build `repoURL` from `gitea-http.gitea.svc:3000` instead of using the clone URL Gitea reports?
options: The in-cluster name is faster to type
Gitea reports a `localhost` URL that only works from your laptop, not from Argo CD inside the hub
Gitea's API returns no clone URL
why: Inside the hub, `localhost` is the Argo CD pod itself. Argo CD must use the in-cluster Service name to reach Gitea.

q: What does `goTemplateOptions: ["missingkey=error"]` protect you from?
options: A template silently rendering an empty value when a label or field is missing
why: Without it, a missing key (for example a cluster without the ring label) renders as empty or `<no value>` and you get a broken Application instead of a clear error.

q: In the Backstage template, what does the `fetch:template` step do?
options: Downloads the template from the internet
Copies the skeleton and fills in the form values (`${{ values.name }}`)
Registers the component in the catalog
why: `fetch:template` renders the skeleton folder with the parameters. `publish:gitea` then creates and pushes the repo, and `catalog:register` adds `catalog-info.yaml` to the catalog.

q: Why do the golden-path selectors use only `name`, `instance` and `part-of`, and not the `tier` label?
options: Kustomize doesn't support more than three labels
A Deployment's selector is immutable, so a label that may change (like tier) must never be in it
Argo CD ignores the tier label
why: Changing a selector later is rejected by the API server. Stable identity labels go in selectors; changeable labels go only on objects and pod templates (`includeSelectors: false`).

q: Every Backstage page showed a red 'Failed to fetch' overlay. What was the cause?
options: The default home page's Random Joke widget calls a public API that returned 503, and the dev overlay shows any error
why: The fix was to disable the widget in `app-config.yaml` (`home-page-widget:home/random-joke: false`). A good reminder: the portal should not depend on random external APIs.

q: How does Backstage find the golden-path template file?
options: A catalog `location` in app-config points at `templates/*/template.yaml`
You upload it in the UI each time
Argo CD pushes it to Backstage
why: Templates are catalog entities of kind `Template`, loaded from catalog locations. When the file was in the wrong folder, the template simply didn't appear.

q: Which guardrail is built into the golden-path template itself (not added later by a policy)?
options: A pinned image tag and the `app.kubernetes.io/part-of` label
why: The paved road makes the safe choice the default: pinned image, standard labels, probes, resources and a locked-down securityContext. That's why tenant-api passed the Lab 5 guardrails without changes.

q: Before running the template, must the `tenant-api` repo already exist in Gitea?
options: Yes, the template only updates existing repos
Yes, and it must be empty
why: The scaffolder creates the repo, pushes the rendered skeleton and registers it. If the repo already exists, publish fails.

q: After Backstage creates the repo, who deploys the service to the cells?
options: The fleet ApplicationSet's scmProvider sees the new repo with `deploy/` and Argo CD syncs it to every cell
why: Backstage only creates the repo. GitOps does the rest: the new repo matches the generator, so Applications appear for each cell automatically.

q: Which statement is correct?
options: Backstage is the source of truth for deployments
Git is the source of truth; Backstage is the portal; Argo CD delivers
Argo CD is the source of truth
The cluster is the source of truth
why: Backstage creates and shows things, but what runs is decided by Git. If Backstage disappeared, deployments would keep working.

q: How does Backstage authenticate to Gitea to create repos?
options: The `integrations.gitea` config with a username and an access token from the `GITEA_TOKEN` environment variable
SSH keys stored in the catalog
why: The token comes from the environment and is never written into a file in Git. In a company this would be a bot account with minimal scope.

q: What must be enabled before RollingSync works?
why: Progressive syncs are an opt-in ApplicationSet controller feature, set in `argocd-cmd-params-cm`, followed by a controller restart.

q: With RollingSync on, what happens to automated sync on each generated Application?
options: It is turned off (`automated.enabled: false`), and the ApplicationSet controller triggers syncs step by step
why: If every app auto-synced on its own, there would be no ordering. The controller takes over and syncs ring 0 first, then ring 1.

q: When does cell-2 (ring 1) start syncing a change?
options: At the same time as cell-1
After every ring-0 Application is Healthy
why: Each RollingSync step waits for the previous step's apps to be Healthy. A Degraded ring 0 stops the rollout.

q: You changed a deployment in the Gitea UI and the checker didn't see a revert. Which commit message did it look for?
options: One starting with `Revert`, as created by `git revert`
why: `git revert` creates a commit like `Revert "Scale tenant-api to 3 replicas"` that records what was undone. A manual edit gives the same files but loses that history.

q: Someone runs `kubectl scale` on an app that has `selfHeal: true`. What happens?
options: Argo CD detects drift and puts the Git value back
The change is pushed to Git
why: selfHeal reconciles the cluster to Git. Changes must go through Git, or they will be undone.

q: Your fix makes cell-1 Healthy. In the same second, cell-2 syncs, but with the old bad commit. Why can that happen?
options: Healthy is not tied to a commit: cell-2 synced the revision Argo CD had last fetched for it, before its refresh
why: A real race seen in Lab 6. Good habit: after a fix, refresh every app before the next ring starts. And keep canaries in each cell as a second line of defence.

q: What is the difference between Audit and Enforce in a Kyverno validate rule?
options: Audit allows the request and records the violation in a PolicyReport; Enforce rejects it
why: Audit first lets you see who would be broken, fix them (and the golden path), then switch to Enforce.

q: A policy moves to Enforce. A pod already running breaks the rule. What happens?
options: It keeps running and shows as fail in the PolicyReport; its next create or change is blocked
why: Admission only runs on create and update. The trap is the next event (eviction, scale-up, new sync): the replacement is denied, as happened to `hello1`.

q: A namespace gets `tenant.lab/id=acme`. What does the generate policy create in it?
why: One label is the whole onboarding. With `synchronize: true`, Kyverno also recreates the objects if someone deletes them.

q: With only the rule `image: "!*:latest"`, which image gets through even though it actually runs latest?
why: No tag means `:latest`, but the string `nginx` doesn't end in `:latest`. That's why the policy got a second rule: `require-image-tag` (`*:*`).

q: A team wants an exception to `require-part-of-label`. What is the better approach?
options: Add their namespace to the policy's exclude list
A separate, time-boxed PolicyException for that workload, reviewed and visible in reports
Switch the policy back to Audit for everyone
why: Editing the shared policy hides the problem forever. A PolicyException is small, owned, reviewable and can expire.

q: The denial message said `autogen-require-part-of` for a Deployment. What is an autogen rule?
options: A rule you must write by hand for each kind
Kyverno automatically applies Pod rules to pod controllers (Deployment, StatefulSet, Job…) by checking their pod template
A rule generated by Argo CD
why: So a bad Deployment is rejected at apply time, not later when its pods fail to be created.

q: The webhook is named `validate.kyverno.svc-fail`. What does `fail` mean?
options: failurePolicy Fail: if Kyverno is unreachable, matching requests are rejected (fail closed)
why: Fail closed is safer but can block deploys during a Kyverno outage. Run it highly available and exclude system namespaces so the cluster can repair itself.

q: Generated NetworkPolicies stayed missing until you added a ClusterRole labelled `rbac.kyverno.io/aggregate-to-background-controller`. Why?
options: Kyverno needs RBAC permission to create the kinds it generates
why: Kyverno's controllers only have the permissions in their aggregated ClusterRoles. To generate a kind, grant it.

q: What is `Rollout`?
options: A kind added by a CRD; the Argo Rollouts controller acts on it
why: CRD + controller = the operator pattern. The CRD makes the YAML valid; the controller runs the canary steps.

q: There is no service mesh or ingress. What does `setWeight: 25` mean with 4 replicas?
options: Exactly 25% of requests go to the canary
1 of 4 pods runs the new version
why: Without a traffic router the weight is approximated by pod counts. Precise per-request weights need Istio, NGINX, ALB or the Gateway API plugin.

q: The bad release's pods stayed Ready. What caught the problem?
options: The AnalysisRun got a non-2xx answer from the canary and the Rollout aborted
why: Health checks show the process is alive; analysis shows it behaves. With `--random-error`, `/readyz` stayed 200 but `/` returned 500.

q: The bad commit is aborted but still in Git. What is the correct recovery?
options: `kubectl edit rollout` to remove the line
`git revert` the bad commit and push
why: Retry runs the same bad version; kubectl edit is drift that selfHeal undoes; deleting causes an outage. Git is the source of truth.

q: Why does the AnalysisTemplate send the header `Connection: close`?
options: Without it the controller reused a keep-alive connection opened when the canary Service still pointed at stable pods, so it tested stable
why: Found while testing: a bad release passed because every measurement was answered by a stable pod. Always check what your test really hits (the hostname in the measurements).

q: Chart `argo-rollouts` 2.43.9 installs controller v1.10.2. Which version should the kubectl plugin have?
why: The chart version is the installer; the app version is the software. Keep the CLI on the same version as the controller.

q: Someone changes `apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1` to `v1alpha2` to 'release a new version'. What happens?
options: Argo CD can't sync: the server has no resource for that group version
why: `apiVersion` is the schema version of the kind, defined by the CRD. Release versions live in the image tag (or, in this lab, the message).

q: After an abort, a stable pod is only 90 seconds old with 0 restarts while its siblings are 9 minutes old. What happened?
options: It's a new pod: a stable pod was removed to make room for the canary, and recreated when stable scaled back to 4
why: Restarted = same name, RESTARTS > 0. New pod = new name, RESTARTS 0. Events show `Created pod` / `Deleted pod`.

q: After an aborted canary, how does Argo CD show the app?
why: The cluster matches Git (Synced), but the Rollout reports Degraded. Git is wrong, not drifted, and the next ring will not start.

q: Why does `Missing()` take `kubernetes.Interface` instead of `*kubernetes.Clientset`?
options: So tests can pass a fake clientset (`fake.NewSimpleClientset`) with no cluster
why: Depend on the interface, not the concrete type. The core logic becomes unit-testable.

q: What exit code should `fleetcheck` return when one cluster is unreachable?
options: It should hang until the cluster is back
why: 0 = all labelled, 1 = findings, 2 = couldn't check a cluster. Scripts and CI rely on exit codes to decide what to do.

q: Goroutines write results with `results[i] = ...` into a slice sized up front. Why is no mutex needed?
options: Each goroutine writes only its own index, so nothing is shared
why: Partitioning the data avoids locks, and the output order stays stable (sorted context names).

q: Why set `rest.Timeout` as well as using `context.WithTimeout`?
options: `rest.Timeout` also bounds the TCP dial and TLS handshake, so one dead cluster can't hang the run
Context timeouts don't work in client-go
why: With 100 cells, one unreachable API server must not decide how long the whole audit takes.

q: How should the CLI list namespaces on a cluster with 5,000 of them?
options: One List call with no limit
Paginate: `Limit: 500` and follow `Continue` until it's empty
why: Pagination keeps responses and memory bounded on large clusters.

q: Turning this CLI into a controller, what replaces repeated `List` calls?
options: Informers (watch + local cache) feeding a work queue, with level-triggered reconcile
why: Informers cut API load, the work queue gives retries and rate limiting, and reconcile makes the logic idempotent.

q: What is the main reason to choose cells over one big cluster per region?
options: A bounded blast radius: a bad deploy, upgrade or noisy tenant affects one cell, not the region
Kubernetes can't run more than one app per cluster
why: The trade-off you accept is fixed overhead per cell (control plane, add-ons, observability).

q: In a cell architecture, what is the placement service?
options: The single source of truth for which tenant lives in which cell
why: The router and the deployment tooling read it. The edge keeps a cached copy so the placement service is not in the request path.

q: Why does a good RFC have a 'Non-goals' section?
options: To say clearly what the proposal will not solve, so scope doesn't creep and reviewers don't expect it
why: Non-goals prevent misunderstandings and keep the decision focused.

q: How do you move a live tenant between cells with no downtime?
options: Stop the tenant, copy, start it again
Replicate data (dual-write or change-data-capture), switch at the router, keep a rollback plan, one tenant at a time
Delete and recreate in the new cell
why: Data first, traffic last, and always a way back.

q: Which option is best for a mix of ordinary tenants and a few regulated (for example FedRAMP) tenants?
options: A cluster per tenant for everyone
Hybrid: shared cells for most, dedicated cells for regulated or very large tenants, all from the same blueprint
why: It keeps cost low for most tenants and gives a real compliance boundary where it's required.

q: In Crossplane, what does the XRD (CompositeResourceDefinition) define?
options: The platform API: the new kind (`Database`) and which fields a developer may set
why: The XRD is the product contract (the menu). The Composition is the recipe behind it.

q: How can the same `Database` API create RDS on EKS but a Postgres pod in this lab?
options: Several Compositions implement the same kind; one is selected by label (for example `provider: local` or `provider: aws`)
Developers write different YAML per cloud
why: The developer's claim stays the same; the platform picks the backend by composition selection.

q: Why is the database password derived with `sha256sum` of the uid instead of `randAlphaNum`?
options: The template re-renders on every reconcile; a random value would change the password each time
why: Compositions must be deterministic. A changing password would break the app every reconcile.

q: Why is the storage size not tied to `spec.size`?
options: A StatefulSet's `volumeClaimTemplates` are immutable, so a resize would reject the whole update (Synced=False)
why: Grow storage with PVC expansion. On clouds the same problem appears as 'forces replacement' fields.

q: The Database is `Synced False` with 'cannot create statefulsets'. What is missing?
options: RBAC: a ClusterRole labelled `rbac.crossplane.io/aggregate-to-crossplane` for the kinds being composed
why: Crossplane v2 can compose any kind, but only with permission for it.

q: Why do you sign an image by digest (`@sha256:…`) and not by tag?
options: A tag can be moved to a different image; a digest identifies exact bytes
why: A signature on a tag would be worthless: someone could push a different image under the same tag.

q: What is an SBOM?
options: A list of every package and component inside the image
why: Like an ingredients list. When a new CVE appears, the SBOM index tells you which images contain the affected package.

q: What does `mutateDigest: true` do in the Kyverno verifyImages rule?
options: Rewrites the pod's image reference to the verified digest, so what was verified is exactly what runs
Deletes the tag from the registry
why: Without it, the tag could be moved between verification and the image pull.

q: Which key goes into Git?
options: Neither: keys go into image labels
why: Anyone may read the public key; only the private key can sign. `.gitignore` blocks `*.key`.

q: The policy matches `idp-lab-control-plane:30880/*`. An unsigned image from Docker Hub is deployed. What happens?
options: It's admitted: the rule doesn't look at other registries
why: Next production step: a rule that allows only the platform registry, and mirror third-party images into it after scanning.

q: Why does Kyverno need `allowInsecureRegistry: true` in this lab?
options: The lab registry speaks plain HTTP, and Kyverno must fetch signatures and attestations from it
why: In production the registry has TLS (Harbor, ECR, ACR) and this setting stays off.

q: Cost per tenant label was impossible until you set `metricLabelsAllowlist` on kube-state-metrics. Why?
options: kube-state-metrics exports no Kubernetes labels by default, so `tenant.lab/id` never reached Prometheus
why: You must allowlist the namespace labels you want as metrics (`namespaces=[tenant.lab/id,team,cost-center]`).

q: In OpenCost results, what is `__unallocated__` when aggregating by `label:tenant.lab/id`?
options: Cost of pods in namespaces without that label: shared platform cost (kube-system, monitoring, …)
why: You decide how to split it, with a documented allocation key, and show idle capacity separately.

q: What is the difference between showback and chargeback?
options: Showback shows each team its cost; chargeback actually bills their budget
Showback is for CPU, chargeback for memory
why: Start with showback so teams trust the numbers before money moves.

q: In Prometheus, the namespace label `tenant.lab/id` appears as which label?
why: kube-state-metrics prefixes `label_` and converts `.` and `/` into `_`.

q: The OpenCost add-on was blocked by your own Lab 5 guardrail. What is the platform way to fix it?
options: Exclude the opencost namespace from the policy
Set `podLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/part-of: opencost}` in the add-on values
why: Platform components follow the same rules as tenants. Fix the component, not the policy.

q: Why bill on requests rather than usage?
options: Requests reserve node capacity whether used or not; billing on them makes teams right-size
why: Show usage next to it so teams see the waste (VPA or Goldilocks recommendations).

q: Team identity's KafkaUser has prefix ACLs on `identity.`. It tries to produce to `payments.ledger`. What happens?
why: Ownership is the naming convention: identity owns `identity.*` and nothing else.

q: Why is `auto.create.topics.enable: false` set?
options: So a topic exists only if someone declared it as code (KafkaTopic), with guardrails
why: Auto-created topics bypass naming rules, partition limits and retention policy.

q: The Kafka topic policy reached a cell before Strimzi was installed. After Strimzi arrives, bad topics are still accepted. What fixes it?
options: Re-apply or change the policy (or restart Kyverno) after the CRDs exist
why: Found while testing: Kyverno kept a stale copy of a policy whose kind didn't exist yet. Order matters: CRDs first, then the policy.

q: How does a client prove its identity to the Kafka cluster in this lab?
options: mTLS: a client certificate issued by the User Operator, stored in a Secret named after the KafkaUser
why: The only listener requires TLS client authentication, so ACLs and quotas apply per identity. No anonymous access.

q: What do KafkaUser quotas (`producerByteRate`, `consumerByteRate`) protect against?
options: A noisy neighbour: one team using all broker capacity on a shared cluster
why: Quotas keep a shared cluster fair. ACLs control who; quotas control how much.

q: This lab uses one broker with replication factor 1. What is a typical production setup?
why: RF=3 with min ISR 2 survives losing one broker without losing acknowledged writes.

q: Scenario: a developer says 'my deploy didn't happen'. What do you check first?
options: The Argo CD Application: sync status, revision and operation message
why: Go top down: Argo CD app → rings (ApplicationSet status) → workload (Rollout/Deployment) → events → logs. Stop at the first red layer.

q: Scenario: Argo CD shows a Rollout Synced but Degraded with 'analysis … failed'. What does it mean?
options: The new version was tested and refused; users are still on stable. Fix Git (revert)
why: This is the canary doing its job. Synced means Git was applied; Degraded means the new version failed analysis.

q: Scenario: a ReplicaSet has 0 pods and events show FailedCreate 'admission webhook … denied'. Which layer is it?
options: Kyverno guardrails: the pod spec breaks a policy (tag, label, signature)
why: Read the policy and rule name in the message, then fix the workload in Git. Running pods are not affected; only new ones.

q: Which pairing is correct?
options: Rings protect each pod; canaries protect the fleet
Rings protect the fleet (cell by cell); canaries protect each cell (pod by pod with analysis)
why: Defence in depth: in Lab 6 a ring gate let a bad commit through by a race, and cell-2's canary still stopped it.
